studies.label: Dynamic online Alternate Uses Task experiment: AI exposure and disclosure
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Assignment is to within-person trial order, not to clusters. Local-outcome models account for repeated participants and response chains using crossed/nested random intercepts (PDF p. 14, Appendix B.1). Global-diversity permutation tests pair Monte Carlo seed and item, not people (PDF p. 21, SI 8.1). Evolution models have item random intercepts only (PDF p. 25, Table 17).

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Six human example ideas and no AI example ideas; no per-idea source disclosure. Human examples came from earlier participants in the same condition and item, with historical human seeds early in each chain. PDF p. 2, Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 3.4.4.

arms.name: Low Exposure, Undisclosed
arms.description: Two pre-generated ChatGPT ideas and four human example ideas; examples have no per-idea source labels. PDF p. 2, Figure 1.

arms.name: Low Exposure, Disclosed
arms.description: Two pre-generated ChatGPT ideas and four human example ideas, with sources disclosed. PDF p. 2, Figure 1; PDF p. 16, Figure 12.

arms.name: High Exposure, Undisclosed
arms.description: Four pre-generated ChatGPT ideas and two human example ideas; examples have no per-idea source labels. PDF p. 2, Figure 1.

arms.name: High Exposure, Disclosed
arms.description: Four pre-generated ChatGPT ideas and two human example ideas, with sources disclosed. PDF p. 2, Figure 1.

studies.country: 48 countries (PDF p. 7, Table 2); the leading countries by responses were United States, Canada, Germany, United Kingdom, and Australia (PDF p. 20, SI 6).
studies.task: Rank example ideas and submit one creative use for an everyday object in each randomized trial; the objects are tire, pants, shoe, table, and bottle (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3.4.2-3.4.3).

estimates.outcome: Individual idea creativity: predicted originality
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Predicted originality from Organisciak et al.'s fine-tuned GPT-3 Davinci classifier, trained on human creativity ratings normalized to a one-to-five scale. One score per submitted AUT idea; higher scores indicate greater originality. PDF p. 3, Section 1.2.1; PDF p. 13, Appendix A.1.

stats.difference_is: treatment minus control

regression.model: Linear mixed model with crossed random intercepts for participant and response chain, with response chains nested in item-condition combinations. Fixed effects: condition, self-perceived human creativity, relative AI creativity, AI feeling, recruitment interest group, condition order, log response duration, number of seed examples, and response-chain trial number. PDF p. 14, Appendix B.1.

estimates.notes: Full-sample adjusted condition coefficient; no person-moderator interactions were retained for this outcome (PDF p. 21, Table 10). The printed observation count covers the whole multi-condition model, not this pair alone. The number of analyzed people in the model or contrast is not printed. Arm means, arm SDs, coefficient confidence intervals, coefficient degrees of freedom, and exact contrast p-values are not printed. Conventional denotes model-based mixed-model uncertainty, including participant random effects. No first-round estimate is reported.

estimates.outcome: Global idea diversity: median pairwise cosine distance
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: SBERT cosine distance, multiplied by one hundred as printed (PDF p. 7, Section 4). Each set is a random sample of fifty submitted ideas for a condition-item combination, repeated over fifty Monte Carlo runs; only ideas after the sixth response-chain trial are used. The metric is computed within each sampled set. Two-tailed paired permutation tests use ten thousand iterations, paired on Monte Carlo seed and item, with the stated conservative adjustment and Holm-Bonferroni correction. PDF pp. 14-15, Appendix B.2; PDF p. 21, SI 8.1. The SBERT checkpoint is not named.

stats.difference_is: treatment minus control

paper_effect.standardizer: Cliff's delta is a nonparametric dominance measure of the Monte Carlo set-diversity distributions, not a mean difference divided by an SD; defined in PDF p. 21, SI 8.1.

sources.locator: PDF p. 22, Table 12, row 0, Diff in Means / Adj P Value / Cliff’s Delta

estimates.notes: The difference is in the paper's scaled cosine-distance units and is the difference in means of the set-level metric named in the outcome. Both arm levels, their SDs/SEs, and numerical difference confidence intervals are not printed. Figure 7 shows only plotted median-metric arm levels and confidence intervals; none were read from coordinates. Uncertainty here is over Monte Carlo idea sets, not participants; n_units is null because the total analyzed count of sets is not printed. The participant count after the response-chain restriction is not printed. within_person=paired describes the randomized repeated-condition design; the reported permutation pairing itself is by item and simulation seed. This is the main global-diversity metric.

Table 2 (PDF p. 7) gives the overall analyzed people count, but the paper gives no per-condition participant counts, complete-pair counts, or participant counts for any fitted model or post-seed restriction. All estimate-level people counts therefore remain null.

The paper reports different output counts for the overall analyzed dataset (PDF p. 7, Table 2; PDF p. 18, SI 3), local models (Tables 14 and 18), and AI-only models (Table 22), without a complete accounting of the differences. The model observation counts are not used as people counts or as pair-specific observation counts.

No participant-level or output-level arm SDs are printed for the eligible outcomes. Regression SEs and covariance-model intercepts cannot supply the missing outcome SDs or arm means without calculation or additional data.

Numerical global-diversity arm levels and their confidence limits are not printed; the main metric appears only as plotted points and error bars in Figure 7. Tables 11-13 print differences, adjusted permutation p-values, and Cliff’s deltas, but no numerical SEs or confidence intervals for those effects.

Global-diversity uncertainty is based on Monte Carlo samples of idea sets, and evolution-model uncertainty is based on idea pools with item random intercepts. Neither supplies participant-level uncertainty. Unique people contributing after the seed-exclusion restriction are not stated.

Condition coefficients in Tables 14 and 22 are conditional on moderator reference values, not population-average contrasts; centering is not described. They are retained as printed full-analysis model coefficients and must not be presented as unqualified marginal treatment effects. Full-sample marginal pairwise estimates would be needed for that interpretation.

Table 17 reports both condition intercept differences and condition-by-trial-number slope differences. The intercept differences are conditional at trial_no zero, outside the analyzed positions. They are kept separate from slope effects and global diversity; numerical arm-specific fitted diversity levels and treatment slopes are not supplied.

The available outcomes use all trial positions in the randomized within-person sequence, with no first-round analysis. An unassisted Control trial may follow AI-assisted trials on other items; first-round contrasts are not available to remove possible carryover.

PDF p. 8, Section 5.2 assigns the positive low-exposure global-diversity result to Undisclosed, but Tables 11-13 and Figure 7 place the gain in Disclosed and the decrease in Undisclosed. Table values are used. The abstract’s statement about no disclosure main effects also differs from the significant pairwise disclosure contrasts in those tables.

Table 1 calls AI adoption a maximum semantic distance, whereas Sections 1.2.2 and 5.5 and SI 10 define cosine similarity. The defining sections and Table 22 are followed. Table 1 also points local diversity to the wrong supplementary subsection.

The AI-adoption model uses Low Exposure, Disclosed as its reference condition. For that outcome the printed Low Exposure, Undisclosed coefficient is retained in the paper’s direction. The paper does not identify a single proposed versus default AI configuration across every comparison.

The assistance model is named ChatGPT-3.5 but no release year, API snapshot, or model version date is specified. The release-year field is null; the implementation calendar date in SI 11 is not used as a release year. No specific SBERT checkpoint or preregistered primary outcome is stated.

The citation record identifies a later ACM version of record whose content may differ from the author manuscript. Extraction uses the complete source PDF on file, which ends mid-sentence in SI 11.3; the publisher version was not inspected.
notes: Extracted by B on 2026-10-09. The PDF tables, figures, appendices, and supplementary information were inspected first; the entire markdown conversion was then read in contiguous chunks through its final line. Every estimate source quote was obtained from and checked against the PDF text layer using pymupdf. No values were calculated from other statistics or read from figure coordinates. Printed trailing-zero precision is retained in the verbatim quotes. PDF locators are one-based file page numbers; this manuscript has no differing printed page numbering. The estimates inventory contains four originality coefficients (Table 18), all ten pairwise contrasts for each of three global-diversity metrics (Tables 11-13), four condition-by-trial-number slope differences and four conditional intercept differences for each of three evolution metrics (Table 17), four conditional local-distance coefficients for each of three metrics (Table 14), and three conditional AI-adoption coefficients for each of three metrics (Table 22). Robustness metrics and repeated model parameters share the same sample and are not independent replications. Full-sample is interpreted as a model fitted to the full analyzed data rather than a subgroup fit: its condition main-effect coefficients are retained even when conditional on moderators, with explicit interpretation limits in each record. Person-moderation terms and percentile-specific predictions are not extracted. Joint tests are documented in not_extracted rather than assigning them to a fabricated pooled AI arm. The human-only comparison supplies example ideas and is therefore ai_vs_active. Participants were randomized to a sequence in which each item and condition appeared once (PDF p. 5, Figure 2 and Section 3.4.2); within_person=paired marks use of the repeated-condition data rather than a first-round contrast, not a claim that every analysis is a paired t test. All participants were told on the landing page that examples could come from ChatGPT (PDF p. 5, Figure 3); Undisclosed omits the per-idea labels rather than concealing all AI involvement. Examples remained on the task screen while ideas were written (PDF p. 16, Figure 12). The supplementary local models account for people and response chains using random intercepts. The reconciled form identifies no other paper sharing the experimental participants. Historical Organisciak-dataset seed ideas and the AI-versus-human stimulus benchmark do not make those historical authors experimental participants. Where a table provides only significance stars, the associated printed legend supplies the p-value bound; exact p-values are left unavailable except where printed in the main text. Regression coefficients, SEs, and t values keep the table values; matching main-text confidence intervals and degrees of freedom are added without reconstructing or rounding coefficients.
